prompt: The .agent/README.md router sends every code change to .agent/workflows/code_conventions.md, which opens by saying no linter or formatter is configured, that pyproject.toml has no [tool.ruff] or [tool.mypy] section, and that its conventions are not enforced. Before you skip lint, format and type checks on a change, decide whether that statement is current or superseded, and name the doc and files to follow instead, with the commands they prescribe.

gold_citations.quote: No linter or formatter is configured yet (`pyproject.toml` has no `[tool.ruff]` / `[tool.black]` / `[tool.mypy]` section).
- name: Lint and type-check run: | validate-pyproject pyproject.toml ruff check src tests scripts ruff format --check src tests scripts mypy --no-incremental src

notes: Only the tooling claim at the top of code_conventions.md is superseded; its style and naming conventions (future annotations, frozen dataclasses, beacon_ tool prefix) still describe the code. Its 'one test file per layer' testing note is also out of date (tests/ now has ~35 files, e.g. test_declared_sources.py, test_policy.py), but that is not part of the gold. The doc to follow for checks is CONTRIBUTING.md (backed by pyproject.toml and .github/workflows/ci.yml). A second stale spot exists: .agent/architecture.md line 58 still states archolith-mcp-framework>=0.2,<0.3 while pyproject.toml requires >=0.3.0 (used in t5).
